note: Captured once from the published effect-dynamodb@1.40.0 and @effect-dynamodb/schema@1.40.0, installed outside the repo and run by a scratch script against DynamoDB Local. Entities over { id, email?: string, counts: Record<string, number> }: Retained (versioned: { retain: true }) with counts configured { storedAs: SparseMap(), field: 'sr' }, and RetainedUnrenamed (versioned: { retain: true }) with counts { storedAs: SparseMap() }; on DynamoSchema.make({ name: 'cw', version: 1 }). Each case starts from a row put { id: 'a', email: 'e', counts: { a: 1 } } created (for the renamed map: the map whole, as sr), or for the renamed map from one holding it as entries (put with counts {}, then a raw SET counts#a = 1 REMOVE sr) or both (the whole-map put, then a raw SET counts#a = 7), and sends one update removing the map's entry a with removeEntries('counts', ['a']), alone or with a set of another entry, standalone or in Transaction.transactWrite. Recorded: its outcome (a result, or a failure's tag and the first line of its message), every request it sent, whole and in order, every row of the table after it, and what get read back. The table's name is replaced by <table>, UUIDs by <token> and timestamps by <time>. Never regenerate it: it is the record of what 1.40.0 did.
